findings.title: Written contract omits approved resolver extensions
findings.problem: The user-approved resolver extensions (Claude version-first reorder, match:'reordered', moonshotai./qwen. prefix stripping, T3 accepting reordered matches, T2 EXCLUDED_MODEL_IDS) were implemented but never written back: spec.md section B/C and AC5/AC9 still mandate exact->snapshot only and six prefixes; docs/ANALYTICS-REPORT.md 'Model pricing resolution' and docs/COMMANDS.md describe two lookup steps only; pricing.json _meta.note still claims a same-tier fallback exists. Acceptance audit reports fail on B lookup order and AC5, partial on canonicalization, PriceResolution, T2, T3, AC9 and section D.
findings.impact: Section D (docs describe resolution rules) is unmet: users and future maintainers read a resolution contract that differs from runtime behaviour, and the spec's fail/partial rows cannot be closed, so the change cannot pass acceptance as recorded.
findings.recommendation: Amend spec.md section B (lookup order step 3, prefix list, PriceResolution.match), section C (T2 exclusion rule, T3 accepting 'reordered'); update the 'Model pricing resolution' section of docs/ANALYTICS-REPORT.md and the pricing note in docs/COMMANDS.md to list the reorder step and moonshotai./qwen. prefixes; remove the stale same-tier-fallback sentence from src/utils/pricing.json _meta.note.

findings.title: Statusline resolver diverges from pricing.ts
findings.problem: statusline.ts carries its own copy of canonicalization/lookupRate documented as mirroring resolvePrice, but it lowercases before stripping and strips bedrock/, converse/ and -vN:N for any id, canonicalizes table keys (strips vendor prefixes and -vertex), and silently overwrites on post-canonicalization key collisions, whereas pricing.ts strips Bedrock prefixes only for *.anthropic.claude-* ids and throws on collisions. statusline.test.ts uses a synthetic table and never compares lookupRate with resolvePrice over priceTable().
findings.impact: For ids outside the anthropic Bedrock shape the live statusline cost and the analytics report can disagree for the same transcript, and a future rule change in one copy only will pass CI. Reachability for Claude-agent traffic was unconfirmed (Claude ids go through the shared anthropic path).
findings.recommendation: Add a parity test in statusline.test.ts asserting lookupRate(priceTable(), id) equals resolvePrice(id)?.price over a list of observed ids (Bedrock/converse, Vertex @-dated, version-first claude, moonshotai./qwen./openai./azure/ prefixes, -vertex, dated gpt-4o, unpriced), and align the normalization and collision handling of the two copies.

findings.title: Codex correlation links newest rollout blindly
findings.problem: On exit the plugin takes recentSessions[0] from rollouts created in the same cwd since start-10s and now records it via recordRolloutCorrelation as correlation.agentSessionFile with status 'matched', unconditionally overwriting any existing correlation. Extra matching rollouts from the same run are ignored.
findings.impact: Two concurrent codex runs in one cwd both correlate to the same rollout, so analytics double-counts its tokens/cost and loses the other run's; extra rollouts from one run are treated as untracked and dropped from the default cost report. This is new because correlation now drives cost attribution.
findings.recommendation: Pick the rollout that belongs to this run (e.g. match rollout session metadata/createdAt against this run's start and exclude rollouts already correlated to another CodeMie session), skip overwriting a different existing agentSessionFile, and warn or record all rollouts when more than one matches.

findings.title: Change grows files already over 500 lines
findings.problem: code-quality.md requires files under 500 lines; this change grows codex.plugin.ts (594->627), otel-loader.ts (563->595), cost-enricher.ts (515->527) and statusline.ts (826->852).
findings.impact: Extends a documented code-structure violation the standards audit treats as blocking, making these modules harder to change.
findings.recommendation: Move the new helpers (recordRolloutCorrelation, the OTEL pricing fallback, statusline canonicalization) into sibling modules, or record an explicit accepted-debt decision.

findings.title: Invalid --export unreported when no sessions
findings.problem: Export-format validation runs after the rawSessions.length === 0 early return, so `--export csv` (or any invalid value) with a filter matching nothing prints 'No sessions found' and exits 0. Separately, a valid-session run with an invalid format still performs full enrichment before the error surfaces.
findings.impact: The documented contract that an invalid format is rejected with a non-zero exit is not honoured on empty result sets; scripts get exit 0 for a bad flag.
findings.recommendation: Validate options.export (and --open) before source.load / the empty-result return, setting process.exitCode = 1 and returning early on an invalid value.

findings.title: --open implies html has no test
findings.problem: No test drives runAnalytics with { open: true } or { open: true, export: 'json' }; grep finds no `open: true`, '--open' or openUrlInBrowser in any test. The --open-implies-html rule replaces the removed --report flag.
findings.impact: Dropping `|| openFlag` or the undefined->html mapping would make the headline `codemie analytics --open` write and open nothing with CI green.
findings.recommendation: In analytics-cli-metadata.test.ts add runAnalytics({ open: true }) asserting generateReport and a mocked openUrlInBrowser are called, and { open: true, export: 'json' } asserting openUrlInBrowser is not called and the notice prints.

findings.title: -o without --export silently ignored
findings.problem: Export resolution runs only when `options.export !== undefined || openFlag`; `codemie analytics -o out.json` leaves exportFormat undefined, writes nothing and prints no warning. The removed --report-output used to imply a report.
findings.impact: Users migrating from --report-output get a successful exit with no file, contradicting the 'clear contract' goal of the task.
findings.recommendation: Include options.output in the condition (default format inferred from the extension, else html) or reject -o without --export/--open with an explicit error and non-zero exit.

findings.title: Generic Error thrown in new code
findings.problem: New code throws plain Error at src/cli/commands/analytics/index.ts:115 ('cost result missing after enrichment') and src/utils/pricing.ts:110 (buildPriceTable key collision). AGENTS.md Common Pitfalls and the git-workflow.md review checklist require specific project error classes.
findings.impact: Violates a documented blocking review-checklist standard; callers cannot distinguish a pricing-data configuration error from other failures.
findings.recommendation: Throw a class from src/utils/errors.ts (e.g. ConfigurationError for the price-table collision); for the index.ts narrowing, restructure so the type narrows without a throw or use a specific error class.

findings.title: Always-on terminal cost wiring untested
findings.problem: analytics-cli-metadata.test.ts mocks AnalyticsFormatter with displayCost = vi.fn() but never asserts it; formatter.test.ts calls displayCost directly; T1 checks only the JSON file.
findings.impact: Removing the displayCost call or passing the source cost instead of the enriched costResult removes the always-on cost summary (AC1) without failing any test.
findings.recommendation: Keep a handle on the mocked formatter and assert displayCost was called with the enrichCosts summary for runAnalytics({}) and runAnalytics({ export: 'json' }).

findings.title: Explicit -o write paths not covered in CI
findings.problem: The only test driving -o file/directory targets through runAnalytics is T1 in the `agent` vitest project, which `npm run ci` and ci.yml never run (vitest.config.ts excludes tests/integration/agent-*.test.ts from `cli`). output-target.test.ts covers only path computation; analytics-cli-metadata.test.ts never passes `output`.
findings.impact: Regressions where options.output stops reaching resolveOutputTargets, mkdirSync is dropped (ENOENT on `-o nested/dir/`), or explicit paths go back through the relocating fallback ship with CI green.
findings.recommendation: Add unit/cli-project tests: runAnalytics({ export: 'both', output: '<tmp>/nested/dir/' }) asserting both files exist, and runAnalytics({ export: 'json', output: '<tmp>/x.json' }) asserting generateReportJson got that path and writeReportWithFallback was not called.

findings.title: OTEL session priced/basis flags not updated
findings.problem: buildCostIndex initializes every session with priced: true and never clears it when events fall through to the new resolver path; unpriced events add $0 and leave priced true. costSource/costBasis are set to authoritative/source-reported only on cost_usd events and never marked when events are table-priced, so a mixed session stays labelled source-reported.
findings.impact: `Priced sessions: n/m` and meta.totals.pricedSessions overcount for OTEL reports, hiding unpriced coverage, and table-estimated dollars are presented as authoritative in the report.
findings.recommendation: Set sc.priced = false when all of a session's usage is unpriced (e.g. derive from perModel after the loop: priced = some model not unpriced), and mark costBasis as mixed/table when any event is priced via resolvePrice.

findings.title: Zero-usage OTEL events flagged unpriced
findings.problem: Any event without cost_usd whose model does not resolve sets eventUnpriced, even when it carries zero tokens; a missing model attribute becomes '(unknown)' and lands in unpricedModels. Docs say only events with usage but no cost_usd are priced through the resolver.
findings.impact: unpricedModels can fill with noise such as '(unknown)', and the task makes a non-empty unpricedModels a build-breaking signal, so this can produce false alarms. Reachability unconfirmed: whether real OTEL api_request events arrive with zero usage or no model was not established.
findings.recommendation: Only mark unpriced when the event's token total is > 0 (and skip or separately report events with no model attribute).

findings.title: OTEL estimated-model path untested
findings.problem: otel-loader.test.ts covers the unpriced (gpt-5.9) and plainly-priced (claude-opus-4-6) fallback paths but never reads summary.estimatedModels or perModel[].estimated; the estimated path is only tested in cost-enricher.
findings.impact: Dropping `if (eventEstimated) estimatedModels.add(model)` or the estimated spread hides tier-estimate pricing in `codemie analytics otel` reports with CI green.
findings.recommendation: Add an otel-loader test: event with model 'claude-opus-4-7', tokens and no cost_usd, asserting summary.estimatedModels equals ['claude-opus-4-7'] and perModel[0].estimated === true; also assert perModel[0].unpriced in the gpt-5.9 case.

findings.title: Dashboard estimated-models logic only regex-tested
findings.problem: report-views.test.ts only regex-matches app.js source for DATA.meta.estimatedModels / m.estimated; neither the cost banner builder nor sessionPayload is executed, although modal-focus.test.ts already runs app.js slices via runInNewContext.
findings.impact: If the banner appends the wrong list or sessionPayload tests m.unpriced instead of m.estimated, the dashboard and per-session JSON export mislabel estimated models while the test passes.
findings.recommendation: Use the vm-slice harness to run sessionPayload on a session with perModelCost [{ model: 'claude-opus-4-7', estimated: true }] and assert meta.estimatedModels, and run the banner builder asserting its text contains 'Estimated models: claude-opus-4-7'.

findings.title: resolvePrice exceeds 50-line function limit
findings.problem: resolvePrice (src/utils/pricing.ts:217-272) is ~56 lines with four near-identical lookup/return blocks; code-quality.md requires functions under 50 lines.
findings.impact: Violates a documented code-structure standard in a newly added exported function; the duplicated blocks also make the lookup order harder to keep in sync with the statusline copy.
findings.recommendation: Extract a helper that tries a key and builds the PriceResolution (key, match), collapsing the four blocks into an ordered candidate list.

findings.title: Task key in commit subjects
findings.problem: 14 of 15 branch commit subjects append '(unify-analytics-cost-command Tn)' or '(Tn)'; git-workflow.md Anti-Patterns forbids a ticket key in the subject when the scope already conveys context.
findings.impact: Branch history does not conform to the documented commit format; a squash PR title carrying the key would land it on main.
findings.recommendation: Move the task reference to the commit body footer and ensure the squash/PR title is '<type>(<scope>): <subject>' without the task key.
